reading.body:
Marketing copy generation dominates this category: of 15 listed tools, roughly two-thirds are oriented toward producing or optimizing promotional text, with SEO scoring and content strategy accounting for most of the remainder.

The concentration is narrow in another dimension as well. Thirteen of the fifteen tools are US-jurisdiction products, with Surfer SEO registered in Poland and Wordtune operated by Israel-based AI21 Labs as the only exceptions. That geographic clustering reflects where the underlying model infrastructure and venture capital have accumulated, consistent with the broader compute geography this site tracks, though the data here covers legal jurisdiction rather than where servers physically sit.

What the data does not cover is notable. There are no figures on inference compute load, energy draw, or data-center footprint for any of these tools. Writing assistance is inference-heavy at scale, processing user documents continuously, but nothing here quantifies that demand. The notes flag that Grammarly "reads document text broadly" and that Typeface uses "brand-customized models," which hints at meaningfully different compute profiles between a grammar corrector and a fine-tuned enterprise model, yet the data stops short of making that comparison concrete. Readers wanting to reason from these tools back to power or building requirements will need sources beyond this list.
